hints: Look closely at how the chromosomes appear in each photo. Which one shows no thick, separate chromosomes, just a dark round nucleus full of grainy chromatin?
Remember when DNA is copied. Semi-conservative replication happens in the S phase of interphase, when DNA is unwound and invisible as chromatin, not during mitosis.
walkthrough:
**Identify what each photo shows**

Look at A, B and D first. You can see thick, dark, condensed chromosomes. That tells you the cell is in mitosis.

A shows chromosomes lined up in the middle, so metaphase. B shows two groups pulled apart, so anaphase. D shows long thin chromosomes becoming visible, so prophase.

**Spot the interphase cell**

Now look at C. There are no individual chromosomes visible. You just see a round nucleus filled with diffuse chromatin.

That decondensed state is the hallmark of interphase, when the cell is not dividing.

**Link replication to S phase**

Semi-conservative DNA replication must happen before mitosis, so each chromosome has two sister chromatids to separate.

It happens in the S phase of interphase, when DNA is unwound and accessible for copying. That matches only photo C.

options.A: This is metaphase, with chromosomes aligned at the equator. No DNA replication happens here, chromosomes are already duplicated and highly condensed.
options.B: This is anaphase, with sister chromatids pulled to opposite poles. DNA was replicated long before this stage.
options.C: This is interphase, with a intact nucleus and decondensed chromatin. The S phase of interphase is when semi-conservative DNA replication occurs.
options.D: This is early mitosis (prophase), with chromosomes condensing and becoming visible. Replication is already complete by this point.
